questions.question: CSS architecture aims to solve:

options.text: Scalability, maintainability, and avoiding style conflicts in large codebases

questions.explanation: As projects grow, ad-hoc CSS becomes unmaintainable; architecture (BEM, ITCSS, modules) brings order and predictability.

questions.question: ITCSS (Inverted Triangle CSS) organizes styles by:

options.text: Specificity/layer — from generic (settings, tools) to specific (components, trumps)

questions.explanation: ITCSS layers from low- to high-specificity (settings→tools→generic→elements→objects→components→utilities) to control the cascade.

questions.question: CSS Modules (in build tooling) provide:

options.text: Locally-scoped class names to avoid global collisions

questions.explanation: CSS Modules hash/namespace class names per file, preventing accidental cross-file clashes in component-based apps.

questions.question: A 'reset' (e.g. normalize.css) primarily:

options.text: Reduces cross-browser inconsistencies in default styles

questions.explanation: Resets/normalizers even out UA defaults so layouts start from a consistent baseline across browsers.

questions.question: Good architecture keeps specificity:

options.text: Low and flat so overrides are predictable (avoid deep selectors/IDs)
As high as possible with IDs
Equal to the number of files

questions.explanation: Low-specificity, single-class selectors keep the cascade predictable and reduce the need for !important.

questions.question: In Angular, component ViewEncapsulation helps architecture by:

options.text: Scoping component styles so they don't leak globally

questions.explanation: Encapsulation scopes styles per component (Emulated by default), a built-in architectural boundary that reduces leaks.

questions.question: The 'utility-first' architecture (Tailwind) trades:

options.text: Semantic class names for composable utility classes in markup

questions.explanation: Utility-first moves styling into atomic classes rather than bespoke semantic classes — different tradeoff vs BEM-style architecture.

questions.question: A maintainable large-scale approach often combines:

options.text: Design tokens (variables) + BEM/Modules + a layering strategy

questions.explanation: Tokens for theming, a naming/scoping convention, and disciplined layering together keep CSS scalable.
